About Bitdeer:

Bitdeer is a world-leading technology company for AI and Bitcoin mining infrastructure.

Bitdeer is committed to providing comprehensive Bitcoin mining solutions for its customers and building AI computational infrastructure to support the AI revolution. Bitdeer handles complex processes involved in computing such as equipment procurement, transport logistics, data center design and construction, equipment management, and daily operations. Bitdeer also offers advanced cloud capabilities to customers with high demand for artificial intelligence.

Headquartered in Singapore, Bitdeer has deployed data centers across multiple countries, including the United States, Norway, Bhutan, and Ethiopia.

To learn more, visit https://ir.bitdeer.com/

We are seeking

We are seeking an experienced Field Application Engineer to lead technical due diligence on data centers for AI and GPU infrastructure deployment. This role is responsible for assessing site readiness, validating usable power and cooling capacity, quantifying gaps and remediation needs, and delivering clear go or no-go recommendations that move qualified sites to deployment. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, detail-driven engineer and clear communicator who thrives in a fast-growing, dynamic environment.

This is a full-time role based in San Jose, CA, with regular travel for on-site assessments and deployment support.

What you will be responsible for

  • Lead remote reviews and on-site inspections of data centers to determine whether they can support target GPU cluster configurations, capacity, and deployment schedules.
  • Validate operator claims against drawings, equipment specifications, operating records, utility documentation, and commissioning evidence.
  • Distinguish utility supply, total facility load, and usable IT capacity, and assess available and committed capacity, rack density, and expansion constraints.
  • Evaluate power distribution, UPS, backup generation, and redundancy against the needs of high-density AI workloads.
  • Assess air cooling and direct-to-chip liquid cooling, including heat rejection, cooling distribution units (CDUs), facility water conditions, flow and temperature, piping, and leak detection.
  • Review rack space, floor loading, delivery access, cabling, carrier diversity, fiber routes, bandwidth, and latency, and partner with network engineering on Ethernet and InfiniBand cluster designs.
  • Review monitoring, maintenance, incident response, remote hands, physical security, and commissioning and acceptance records to identify operational and resilience gaps.
  • Classify sites as ready for deployment, requiring defined upgrades, or requiring substantial development.
  • Produce decision-ready assessments documenting achievable IT capacity, rack count, dependencies, cost estimates, schedule risks, and a go or no-go recommendation.
  • Resolve technical questions with operators, landlords, utilities, equipment vendors, and contractors.
  • Define remediation and acceptance criteria, verify closure of critical issues, and hand development work to the appropriate team.
  • Partner with AI ecosystem, cloud infrastructure, procurement, and engineering teams to build a consistent assessment process and a prioritized pipeline of qualified sites.

How you will stand out

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years of experience in data center engineering, critical facilities, infrastructure solutions engineering, commissioning, or field applications engineering.
  • Hands-on experience assessing or delivering data centers, with a track record of identifying deployment blockers and driving technical issues to resolution.
  • Strong working knowledge of electrical and mechanical infrastructure, including power distribution, backup systems, cooling, and the relationship between facility capacity and usable IT load.
  • Ability to read electrical single-line diagrams, mechanical schematics, equipment data sheets, rack layouts, and commissioning reports.
  • Understanding of AI or HPC infrastructure requirements, including high-density GPU systems, liquid cooling, and high-speed networking.
  • Ability to write clear site assessment reports, compare options, estimate remediation scope, and explain technical risks and tradeoffs to business stakeholders.
  • Strong professional English communication skills and willingness to travel for site assessments and deployment support.
  • Preferred: experience with GPU cloud, colocation, hyperscale, or HPC facilities, including high-density or liquid-cooled deployments.
  • Preferred: experience with facility commissioning, integrated systems testing, capacity planning, or converting existing facilities for AI workloads.
  • Preferred: familiarity with colocation agreements, service-level commitments, utility tariffs, power usage effectiveness (PUE), and total cost of ownership (TCO).
  • Preferred: experience coordinating equipment vendors, data center operators, and engineering contractors across regions.

What you will experience working with us

  • A culture that values authenticity and diverse perspectives.
  • An inclusive, respectful environment with open workspaces and an energetic, start-up spirit.
  • A fast-growing company with opportunities to network with industry pioneers and enthusiasts.
  • The ability to contribute directly and make an impact on the future of the digital asset and AI computing industry.
  • Involvement in new projects and in developing processes/systems.
  • Personal accountability, autonomy, rapid growth, and learning opportunities.
  • Attractive benefits and development such as training and mentoring.

Interviewing with TRM

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

You will maintain deep relationships with Members of Congress, committee staff, key federal regulators, and the Executive Branch — building and executing legislative and regulatory strategies on issues central to Stripe's mission, including payments modernization, financial regulation, artificial intelligence, and the future of agentic commerce.   • At least 12+ years of experience in a policymaking, government, or senior advocacy role — ideally a mix of time on Capitol Hill, in a federal regulatory agency, or in a world-class organization as an in-house government relations expert or other business-related role
  • A background working for a Member of Congress, a committee or leadership office, or in a senior policy role at the US Treasury, OCC, FDIC, White House, or comparable federal institution — with a track record of navigating bipartisan legislative environments
  • Deep expertise in financial services regulation and payments policy, with a strong understanding of the legislative and regulatory landscape across banking, money transmission, and digital assets
  • Familiarity with, and ideally direct experience on, emerging technology policy — including artificial intelligence, agentic commerce, and the regulatory questions that arise at the intersection of AI and financial services
  • Strong relationships with policymakers and staff on both sides of the aisle and a reputation for credibility, reliability, and good judgment

  • Passion for Stripe's mission of helping businesses grow and thrive
  • A collaborative, curious team-first mindset with experience thriving in ambiguous, high-growth or startup environments across global offices.

About Coinflow

Coinflow is the next-generation payment service provider revolutionizing global financial infrastructure with stablecoins, AI-driven fraud prevention, and instant settlement. Coinflow enables businesses to grow faster with instant settlement, fraud & chargeback indemnity, global pay-ins, multi-currency FX, and unified payouts. Founded in 2023, the company serves marketplaces, fintechs, remittance providers, gaming platforms, and ecommerce merchants worldwide.

Since our seed round in 2024, we’ve achieved 23x revenue growth and scaled to multi-billion-dollar annual transaction volume. In response to this growth, Coinflow announced a $25M Series A in October 2025—led by Pantera Capital, CMT Digital, Coinbase Ventures, Jump Crypto, and Reciprocal Ventures—accelerating our mission to power the world’s fastest-moving businesses with innovative, reliable global payments.

Coinflow is proudly headquartered in Chicago, IL. Learn more at coinflow.cash.

About the Role

As we scale, we're making our first dedicated chargeback & fraud hire, a hands-on practitioner who will build our fraud function from the ground up: fraud tooling, investigations workflow, alert triage, and bank-partner reporting.

This role reports to our Risk Manager within the broader Risk & Compliance organization, and requires 5–8 years of relevant experience.

This is a builder role, not a maintainer role. You'll be the fraud subject-matter expert inside Coinflow, working alongside our BSA/AML Officer, Underwriters and Data Science, and will be the primary point of contact for fraud-related RFIs from our sponsor bank partners.

What You'll Do

Build the fraud function

  • Further develop and mature our existing transaction monitoring tool and investigations workflow, including case management, alerting logic, and evidence documentation standards.

  • Define SOPs, escalation paths, and decision frameworks for fraud investigations as the team's first dedicated hire.

Work alerts, investigations, and remediation

  • Monitor and triage fraud alerts across merchant and user/cardholder populations, investigating transaction patterns, account activity, and behavioral signals.

  • Conduct deep-dive investigations into suspected fraudulent merchants, card testing, account takeover, ACH fraud, and related fraud typologies.

  • Drive remediation: case disposition, funding actions, merchant/user offboarding recommendations, and root-cause analysis on confirmed fraud losses.

Identify and manage fraud risk vectors

  • Continuously assess Coinflow's exposure across merchant fraud (fraudulent merchant onboarding, bust-out schemes, transaction laundering) and user fraud (ATO, card testing, CNP fraud, ACH fraud, scams).

  • Track chargeback and fraud trends specific to our high-risk verticals (crypto on/off-ramps, gaming, remittance, digital goods) and recommend controls.

  • Monitor card network programs (VAMP, ECM/HECM, EFM, VIRP, BRAM, and new programs as they launch), in addition to NACHA program requirements, manage merchant remediation to stay below thresholds, and build workflows to meet new program requirements.

  • Track industry developments, network rule changes, and regulatory updates, and translate them into product and control recommendations.

Bank partner & stakeholder engagement

  • Serve as the primary owner of fraud-related RFIs from sponsor bank partners, preparing data, narratives, and supporting documentation.

  • Partner with the BSA/AML Officer and Data Science to align fraud and AML signal-sharing and investigations.

  • Present fraud metrics, trends, and program updates to Risk & Compliance leadership.

Operational Leadership (as the team grows)

  • Hire, train, and mentor fraud analysts.

  • Build out queue SLAs, escalation paths, and QA/calibration of analyst decisions.

  • Own the fraud playbooks and procedures.

Requirements

  • 5–8 years of experience in chargeback & fraud prevention, detection, investigations, or remediation within a payment service provider, Acquirer, or fintech platform.

  • Strong, hands-on understanding of fraud in the card acquiring space, covering both:

  • Merchant fraud: Fraudulent merchant onboarding/boarding fraud, transaction laundering, bust-out schemes, collusive merchant activity.

  • User/cardholder fraud: Account takeover (ATO), card testing, card-not-present (CNP) fraud, scams and social engineering.

  • Working knowledge of card brand fraud and chargeback monitoring programs such as VAMP, ECM, SMMP, VIRP, BRAM, etc., and experience remediating merchants against these thresholds.

  • Experience building or significantly improving fraud tooling, case management workflows, or investigations processes. This is a builder, not just an operator.

  • Comfortable responding directly to bank partner and sponsor bank RFIs, including preparing data and written narratives.

  • Highly analytical; comfortable using data to identify emerging fraud trends and to justify policy or tooling changes.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Able to explain complex fraud findings clearly to non-fraud stakeholders and external partners.

  • Sound judgment and ability to make and stand behind difficult, sometimes ambiguous, fraud decisions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with high-risk or emerging verticals such as crypto on/off-ramps, gaming, sweepstakes, digital goods.

  • SQL proficiency or comparable data skills to build dashboards, track fraud metrics, and drive investigations independently.

  • Familiarity with AML/KYC/underwriting processes and how fraud and onboarding signals intersect in a payments risk organization.

  • People leadership experience or a demonstrated path toward building and leading a fraud team over time.

  • Comfortable discussing complex merchant processing situations with Acquirers, Sponsor Banks, and the Card Networks.

The base salary range for this role is $130,000 – $170,000 USD + equity. The actual base salary offered depends on a variety of factors, including but not limited to experience, education, skills, qualifications, and business needs.

Join the team rewriting how money moves worldwide—and become a driving force in the $194 trillion cross-border payments market.
